Das Dunkelglasviertel: Was der Junge sah: The Darkglass Quarter: What the Boy Saw
„Mein Junge hat die schwarzen Laternen a: "My boy lit the black lanterns, every evening, the way I taught him. Since then he sees things that haven't happened yet. Three nights ago he ran off because he saw who is coming. Please find him."
In dem Heft, das du dem Rivalen abgenomm: In the notebook you took from the rival, the boy wrote down where he is hiding: in the cellar beneath the guild board. Elsa runs off. Later she comes back holding his hand and presses her savings into yours. "He says you will go far. He doesn't like saying it."
Am Ende der Gassen liegt, was noch fehlt: At the end of the alleys lies what was still missing. Whoever left it here is long gone.
Dem Rivalen das letzte Stück abnehmen: Take the last piece from the rival
Das Dunkelglasviertel: Eine Kindermütze: The Darkglass Quarter: A child's cap
Unter einer schwarzen Laterne liegt eine: Under a black lantern lies a cap with a note inside in a child's hand: "I saw who is coming. He walks the same way as the stranger."
Eine Laterne mit Kreide auf das Pflaster: A lantern drawn in chalk on the cobbles, shining downwards. Next to it an arrow into the alleys. The boy wanted to be found.
Das Dunkelglasviertel: Eine zerbrochene: The Darkglass Quarter: A broken lamp pole
Die Stange des Jungen, zerbrochen. Daneb: The boy's pole, broken. Next to it fresh boot prints, and a smell you know: a Beyonder of your own pathway was here before you.
„Ich habe einen Faden berührt und bin mi: "I touched a thread and woke up with someone else's memories. I know how his wife laughs. My own I have forgotten. Somewhere my thread is still hanging. Help me find it."
Auf der Spule, die du dem Rivalen abgeno: Jost's name is on the spool you took from the rival. He holds it to his forehead and weeps. "Her name is Marthe. She laughs like a kettle boiling over." He gives you everything he has.
Das Garnviertel: Ein verknoteter Faden: The Yarn Quarter: A knotted thread
Zwischen zwei Häusern hängt ein Faden mi: Between two houses hangs a thread with a hundred knots. Each knot a name. Jost's is not among them, but the thread leads downwards.
Das Garnviertel: Ein Spinnrad: The Yarn Quarter: A spinning wheel
Ein Spinnrad mitten im Hof, das sich von: A spinning wheel in the middle of the yard, turning by itself. It spins memories into yarn. One spool is missing.
Hier hat jemand Fäden abgeschnitten und: Someone has cut threads here and pocketed them, cleanly, with a blade of your own pathway. Whoever it was is collecting other people's memories.
Das Larvenviertel: Das eigene Gesicht: The Mask Quarter: One's Own Face
„Ich habe mein Gesicht zum Trocknen ins: "I hung my face in the window to dry, like everyone here. In the morning it was gone. Without a face my daughter no longer knows me. Please, bring it back to me."
Die Frau setzt ihr Gesicht auf, und es s: The woman puts on her face, and it fits at once. A girl runs out of a door and throws her arms around her neck. The woman smiles at you, for the first time with her own mouth, and gives you a whole year's wages.
Das Larvenviertel: Ein leeres Fenster: The Mask Quarter: An empty window
Ein Haken, an dem kein Gesicht mehr häng: A hook with no face hanging on it any more. Beneath it footprints that wear different shoes with every step.
Das Larvenviertel: Ein Haufen Gesichter: The Mask Quarter: A pile of faces
In the yard a pile of discarded faces. None fits the description. Someone rummaged through them and took only one.
Das Larvenviertel: Ein Spiegelsplitter: The Mask Quarter: A mirror shard
Im Splitter siehst du kurz ein Gesicht,: In the shard you briefly see a face that is not yours, and behind it someone very much like you: a Beyonder of your pathway who collects faces.
Das Hallviertel: Das dritte Echo: The Hall Quarter: The Third Echo
„Jeder Laut kommt hier dreimal zurück, d: "Every sound comes back three times here, the third time with strange words. I have listened. The third echo speaks of a bell beneath the quarter that no one may ring. And someone is looking for it."
Bruder Anselm nimmt den Klöppel und wieg: Brother Anselm takes the clapper and weighs it in both hands. "Then she stays silent. Good." He sinks it in the guild's deepest well and pays you from the offering box.
Das Hallviertel: Eine Stimmgabel: The Hall Quarter: A tuning fork
Eine Stimmgabel, die summt, ohne dass si: A tuning fork that hums without anyone striking it. It grows louder when you walk towards the alleys.
Das Hallviertel: Ein Gitter im Boden: The Hall Quarter: A grate in the ground
Durch das Gitter hörst du das dritte Ech: Through the grate you hear the third echo clearly: "The clapper is gone. Without the clapper she is silent. With the clapper she wakes everyone."
Untersuchen: Ein Gitter im Boden: Examine: A grate in the ground
Jemand hat hier etwas Schweres weggeschl: Someone dragged something heavy away here. The marks still ring, and the third echo names no stranger but someone of your own pathway.
Das Sudviertel: Das Rezept des Nachbarn: The Brew Quarter: The Neighbour's Recipe
„Was in den Pfützen schwimmt, war einmal: "What swims in the puddles used to be a neighbour. My neighbour, Hannes. He brewed a recipe that was meant to bring someone back, and then he fell into the pot himself. His recipe book is gone. Without it he stays soup."
Greta braut nach Hannes' Buch, mit Gedul: Greta brews from Hannes' book, with patience and no substitutes. In the evening a wet, confused man sits at her table and eats her soup without asking what is in it. Greta pays you with everything in the till.
Das Sudviertel: Eine kochende Pfütze: The Brew Quarter: A boiling puddle
In der Pfütze treibt eine Brille. Hannes: A pair of spectacles drifts in the puddle. Hannes wore them, Greta says. Next to it a torn-out page: "Ingredient three: patience. Do not substitute."
Das Sudviertel: Ein umgestürzter Kessel: The Brew Quarter: An overturned cauldron
Der Kessel ist leer, aber noch warm. Am: The cauldron is empty but still warm. On the rim the fingerprints of someone who lifted something heavy out.
Das Sudviertel: Fremde Zutatenreste: The Brew Quarter: Foreign ingredient scraps
Hier hat jemand gebraut, schnell und sch: Someone brewed here, quickly and sloppily, with ingredients of your own pathway. Whoever it was wants the recipe for themselves.
Das Nietenviertel: Der Rost auf der Haut: The Rivet Quarter: Rust on the Skin
"The rust is growing on my apprentices. First the hands, then the arms. The guild had an oilstone that holds back the rust. Since the walls started moving closer at night, it has disappeared."
Meister Hammerl reibt seinen Lehrlingen: Master Hammerl rubs his apprentices' hands with the oilstone. The rust flakes off like old paint. He doesn't forge for you, he pays. "I can't offer you better work than what you can already do."
Das Nietenviertel: Eine verrostete Zange: The Rivet Quarter: A rusted pair of tongs
Die Zange eines Lehrlings, halb zu Rost: An apprentice's tongs, half crumbled to rust. On them an oil stain, fresh, dripping towards the alleys.
Untersuchen: Eine verrostete Zange: Examine: A rusted pair of tongs
Das Nietenviertel: Eine eingedrückte Tür: The Rivet Quarter: A dented door
Die Wände haben diese Tür in der Nacht z: The walls crushed this door in the night. Behind it an empty velvet pouch that once held something heavy.
Jemand hat hier die Wände mit bloßer Kra: Someone pried the walls apart here with bare strength, the strength of your own pathway. The oilstone is not lost, it is stolen.
Das Türenviertel: Der Weg in die Küche: The Door Quarter: The Way to the Kitchen
Herr Pölz, sucht seit sieben Jahren sein: Mr Pölz, has been looking for his kitchen for seven years
"Every door leads somewhere other than yesterday. I have been looking for my kitchen for seven years. I know there is a master key that leads every door to where it belongs. The guild lost it. Or sold it."
Herr Pölz steckt den Hauptschlüssel in d: Mr Pölz puts the master key in the nearest door and turns it. Behind it there is a smell of onions. "My kitchen!" He gives you the contents of his pantry and his savings stocking, seven years' worth.
Das Türenviertel: Eine Tür ins Nichts: The Door Quarter: A door to nowhere
Hinter der Tür nur eine Mauer, darauf in: Behind the door only a wall, with chalk on it: "The key is below. Don't ask which door."
Das Türenviertel: Ein Schlüsselbrett: The Door Quarter: A key board
Hundert Haken, hundert Schlüssel. Ein Ha: A hundred hooks, a hundred keys. One hook is empty, and it is the largest.
Das Türenviertel: Ein aufgebrochenes Sch: The Door Quarter: A forced lock
Kein Dietrich, kein Werkzeug: Das Schlos: No lockpick, no tool: the lock opened itself, for someone of your own pathway. You are not the first to look for the master key.
Das Gewichtsviertel: Die Schuld der Leic: The Weight Quarter: The Debt of the Light
Edda Kornfeld, Witwe eines Schuldners: Edda Kornfeld, widow of a debtor
„Mein Mann konnte nicht zahlen, also wur: "My husband couldn't pay, so he grew lighter until the wind took him. His debt is written in a book of the guild. If it is struck out, he comes back. The book has disappeared."
Edda streicht die Zeile mit zitternder H: Edda strikes out the line with a trembling hand. Outside someone falls from the sky into the gutter and curses. Edda laughs and weeps and pays you with the money that no one owes any more.
Das Gewichtsviertel: Eine Feder an einer: The Weight Quarter: A feather on a string
An einem Laternenpfahl flattert eine Fed: A feather on a string flutters from a lamppost. A name is on it: Kornfeld. He is not quite gone yet.
Untersuchen: Eine Feder an einer Schnur: Examine: A feather on a string
Das Gewichtsviertel: Eine leere Waagscha: The Weight Quarter: An empty scale pan
Die Waage im Hof ist aus dem Gleichgewic: The scale in the yard is off balance. On the empty side a book once lay, heavy enough to hold an entire alley.
Eine Quittung, unterschrieben von jemand: A receipt, signed by someone of your own pathway: "Debt ledger taken over. Payment will never follow." Someone wants to collect the quarter's debts.
Das Faulviertel: Was die Straße festhält: The Rot Quarter: What the Street Holds
„Die Straßen erinnern sich an jeden, der: "The streets remember everyone who has walked them, and some they hold on to. My sister has been stuck up to her hips in peat for weeks. There was a bog light that makes the street let go. It went out, or someone took it."
Lene hält das Moorlicht über den Torf. D: Lene holds the bog light over the peat. The street sighs and releases her sister, wet and laughing. The two of them give you a whole peat season's wages.
Das Faulviertel: Ein Torfstecher: The Rot Quarter: A peat spade
Lene's spade, stuck in the ground. The peat beneath is warm and whispers names.
Das Faulviertel: Eine leere Laterne: The Rot Quarter: An empty lantern
Eine Moorlaterne ohne Licht. Am Glas Spu: A bog lantern without light. On the glass the marks of fingers that had no fear of the bog.
Das Faulviertel: Fußspuren, die nicht ei: The Rot Quarter: Footprints that don't sink
Jemand ist hier über den Torf gegangen,: Someone walked across the peat here without sinking. Only someone of your own pathway can do that. The bog light went with them.
Das Stillviertel: Die stehengebliebene S: The Still Quarter: The Stopped Hour
„Die Zeit läuft hier in Stücken, seit je: "Time here runs in pieces since someone tore the balance wheel out of the guild clock. My father has been standing mid-step on the boulevard for a year. Without the balance wheel he will never arrive."
Thea setzt die Unruh ein. Auf dem Boulev: Thea fits the balance wheel. On the boulevard her father sets his foot down, a year late, and asks why everyone looks so old. Thea pays you with the most expensive watch in her shop and all the money she has.
Das Stillviertel: Ein Mann mitten im Sch: The Still Quarter: A man mid-step
Theas Vater, erstarrt, ein Bein in der L: Thea's father, frozen, one leg in the air. In his hand a pocket watch running backwards, towards the alleys.
Das Stillviertel: Zahnräder im Rinnstein: The Still Quarter: Cogs in the gutter
Zahnräder, verstreut wie Brotkrumen. Sie: Cogs, scattered like breadcrumbs. They all turn, except one that is broken.
Das Stillviertel: Eine angehaltene Sekun: The Still Quarter: A held second
Hier steht eine einzige Sekunde still in: Here a single second hangs still in the air, and in it the imprint of a hand of your own pathway. Someone stole the balance wheel to make time run for themselves.
